question: My CRA account's displayed TFSA contribution room does not yet reflect a recent withdrawal. Which records should I use to avoid making an excess contribution?
generated_answer:
You may use either your official Statement of Account or the Tax Information Summary. Note that the Tax Information Summary is more detailed and may be easier to use. The CRA updates both records on a regular basis. How do I get my TFSA information? How do I get my TFSA information? You can access your TFSA information online through My Account or the MyCRA mobile app. You can also register for direct deposit to receive your CRA payments directly into your bank account. How do I change my TFSA information? How do I change my TFSA information? If you have moved and your address has changed, you must inform the CRA and your TFSA issuer of your new address. You may update your address on My Account or through the MyCRA mobile app. Note that if you change your address, you must also inform the CRA of your new banking information if you have registered for direct deposit. For more information, please see Updating your banking information. What happens if I make an excess TFSA contribution? What happens if I make an excess TFSA contribution? The CRA will impose a penalty tax on the amount of your excess TFSA contributions. This tax is 1% per month, and it will apply for each month that the excess contribution remains in your account. If you make a withdrawal for the excess amount, the penalty tax will be calculated based on the number of months that the excess amount was in your TFSA. Note that if you contribute an amount to your TFSA that is more than your available contribution room, you may receive a warning letter from the CRA. For more information, please see Tax on excess TFSA contributions. I received a warning letter from the CRA. What do I do? I received a warning letter from the CRA. What do I do? If you have received a warning letter from the CRA, you may need to withdraw the excess amount from your TFSA. You should also review your contribution records to make sure that you are not making excess contributions in the future. Note that if you have not withdrawn the excess amount, you may receive a Notice of Determination from the CRA, which will confirm the amount of the penalty tax that you must pay. For more information, please see Tax on excess TFSA contributions. What happens if I do not withdraw my excess TFSA contribution? What happens if I do not withdraw my excess TFSA contribution? If you do not withdraw the excess amount from your TFSA, the CRA will impose a penalty tax on the amount of the excess contribution. This tax is 1% per month, and it will apply for each month that the excess amount remains in your account. Note that if you make a withdrawal for the excess amount, the penalty tax will be calculated based on the number of months that the excess amount was in your TFSA. For more information, please see Tax on excess TFSA contributions. I withdrew my excess TFSA contribution. Will I still be charged a penalty tax? I withdrew my excess TFSA contribution. Will I still be charged a penalty tax? If you have withdrawn the excess amount from your TFSA, you will not be charged a penalty tax. However, you may still be required to pay the penalty tax if you have not withdrawn the excess amount within the time limit specified by the CRA. For more information, please see Tax on excess TFSA contributions. I received a Notice of Determination from the CRA. What do I do? I received a Notice of Determination from the CRA. What do I do? If you have received a Notice of Determination from the CRA, you must pay the penalty tax specified in the notice. The notice will also include information on how to make the payment. Note that if you do not pay the penalty tax, the CRA may take further action, such as seizing your TFSA assets. For more information, please see Tax on excess TFSA contributions. I received a Notice of Assessment from the CRA. What do I do? I received a Notice of Assessment from the CRA. What do I do? If you have received a Notice of Assessment from the CRA, you must pay the penalty tax specified in the notice. The notice will also include information on how to make the payment. Note that if you do not pay the penalty tax, the CRA may take further action, such as seizing your TFSA assets. For more information, please see Tax on excess TFSA contributions. - Online through My Account or the MyCRA mobile app

- By phone using the CRA's automated telephone service

- By mail using a payment voucher

- In person at a CRA office or at a participating financial institution
